# Pneumatic Valve A pneumatic valve is a bidirectional valve controlled by a control pressure.
A pneumatic valve has 3 connections: inlet, outlet, and control. The "input" side is whichever inlet or outlet connection has the higher pressure, and it can switch between the two sides, making the valve bidirectional.
The valve will [color=green]open[/color] when the pressure on the outlet side is at least [color=orange][protodata="PressureControlledValve" comp="PressureControlledValve" member="Threshold"/] kPa[/color] below the pressure on the control side.
The valve will [color=red]close[/color] again when the pressure on the outlet side comes within [color=orange][protodata="PressureControlledValve" comp="PressureControlledValve" member="Threshold"/] kPa[/color] of the pressure on the control side.
For example, a pneumatic valve with a control pressure of 500 kPa will open when the outlet pressure is 500 kPa - [color=orange][protodata="PressureControlledValve" comp="PressureControlledValve" member="Threshold"/] kPa[/color] or lower, and close when the outlet pressure is 500 kPa - [color=orange][protodata="PressureControlledValve" comp="PressureControlledValve" member="Threshold"/] kPa[/color] or higher.
The valve's control pressure is determined by its connection to a pipenet, so it can be adjusted on the fly with a [textlink="pump" link="Pumps"] or another source of pressure control.
## Differences from Pumps
A pneumatic valve differs from a [textlink="pump" link="Pumps"], which performs work to move gas. A pneumatic valve is a passive device that uses the higher pressure of its input gas to move it, so it can sometimes fill volumes faster than a [textlink="pump" link="Pumps"].
For example, a pneumatic valve with a control pressure of 500 kPa will fill a volume faster than a pressure [textlink="pump" link="Pumps"] set to 500 kPa. However, the [textlink="pump" link="Pumps"] can maintain the pressure in the volume more precisely.
A pneumatic valve can be used for a variety of purposes, including: - Automatically venting gases from a combustion chamber through the control inlet - Rapidly filling a volume based on an adjustable control pressure
